request.user:
Subject: Botany
Question type: single-correct (exactly one option is right)

The absolute refractory period during an action potential generation is primarily caused by:
(A) Closure of voltage-gated K^+ channels.
(B) Inactivation of voltage-gated Na^+ channels.
(C) Increased permeability to Cl^− ions.
(D) Continuous activation of the Na^+/K^+ pump.

result.working: During the absolute refractory period no second action potential can be fired, however strong the stimulus. This is because the voltage-gated Na+ channels have entered an inactivated state (inactivation gate closed). They cannot reopen until the membrane repolarises and the channels reset to the closed-but-activatable state. K+ channel kinetics mainly shape the relative refractory period. Cl- permeability and the Na+/K+ pump do not cause refractoriness.
result.note: The question is labelled Botany, but the topic is neural physiology, which is Zoology.
